title: Pod starter: hire + immersion checklist (WIP)
content:
Purpose
---
Working draft playbook to hire and ramp a two-engineer + one-ML eng pod (product + infra adjacent). Primary goals: compress time-to-impact, keep cognitive load low for manager, surface early risk signals for model-serving and infra dependencies.

Context and constraints
- Hiring window: target offer accept by 2026-01-15 to align with Q1 product sprint.
- Budget: 2 ICs (senior SWE + ML infra), 1 IC (product engineer) — budgeted as two L4/L5 and one L3/L4 depending on pipeline.
- Diversity target: at least one of the three hires from underrepresented pools.
- Ramp expectation: first PR with infra-safe changes by week 4, owning small end-to-end feature by week 12.

Sections in this doc
1) Quick hiring plan and interview rubric (scorecard + 3-stage loop)
2) Offer calibration and comp notes
3) Week-by-week immersion checklist for manager, new hires, and people ops
4) Quick decision log, open questions, and TODOs.

1) Hiring plan + interview rubric (compact)
- Role buckets (quick):
  - Pod SWE (service + product feature work) — focus: system design for small services, API ergonomics, testing, shipping fast
  - ML Infrastructure Engineer — focus: inference runtime familiarity, model serving reliability, KV cache & batching nuance, GPU infra understanding
  - Product Engineer — focus: product-facing integrations, telemetry, SLO-aware UX

Interview loop (3 stages)
- Stage A: Phone screen (30m) — culture fit, communication, high-level technical fit, candidate questions. Owner: recruiting + hiring manager. Score: pass/conditional/fail.
- Stage B: Take-home + code review (take-home optional for senior candidates). Candidate given dataset + small infra task: mock inference endpoint + integration test + README. Reviewer: 2 engineers (one infra-focused, one product-focused). Scoring matrix below.
- Stage C: Onsite (half-day, virtual accepted) — deep system design (45m), debugging pair (40m), behavioral + career goals (25m). Hiring manager + 2 interviewers.

Scoring rubric (normalized 0-5) — simple matrix to produce composite decision
- Problem decomposition (0-5): Can break down feature into components, prioritize trade-offs
- Implementation craft (0-5): Code clarity, testing, edge-case handling
- System thinking (0-5): Latency, cost, caching, fallback strategies
- Team fit + communication (0-5)
- Bias for ownership (0-5): shipping signals, maintaining production artifacts
- Accessibility & security awareness (0-5): basic checklist (auth, secrets, PII handling)

Passing rule (working): average >= 3.8 across core categories AND no 0s in security/PII. Hire manager veto allowed with written justification.

Notes on take-home (practical):
- Keep it small: ~3 hours to complete. Provide a Dockerfile and small sample data. Focus on correctness and explanation rather than micro-optimization.
- Include a short prompt: "Implement a simple inference shim that accepts prompt batches, responds with deterministic transform, and include a short explanation of how you'd make it production-grade."
- Reviewer checklist: reproducible run, README clarity, test coverage, notes on trade-offs.

2) Offer calibration and comp guidance (quick)
- Use current band chart (see linked compensation spreadsheet). For senior ML infra hire prioritize equity tilt + signing to compensate longer notice periods.
- Flex levers: start date flexibility, remote stipend, relocation support (rare).
- Hiring manager must run comp check with People Ops < 48hrs of verbal offer.

3) Immersion and 12-week checklist (split by role)
Manager pre-boarding (2 weeks before start):
- Create folder in repo: onboarding/<new-hire-name>/ and seed with 1-2 small starter issues.
- Arrange key intros: SRE, model ops, product PM, security.
- Ensure access: GitHub, JIRA, dev VPC, slack, VPN, GCP/AWS project billing role, secret access request queued.

Day 0-1 (orientation):
- People Ops: benefits, payroll, compliance forms.
- Manager: 30m role expectations sync + 30m 1:1 scheduling for first 90 days.
- Team: lunch intro (virtual ok), low-pressure 1-hr demo of current pod projects.

Week 1: Immerse + small wins
- Dev environment: run local service end-to-end (self-guided doc + 1 pairing session).
- Complete safety/PII training and infra oncall orientation.
- Starter issue assigned: bugfix or doc improvement that touches runtime config.
- Quick checklist: add to runbook, add to Slack channels, create personal dev branch.

Weeks 2-4: Deliver first PRs
- Focus: ship a non-user-facing change (config, tests, telemetry).
- Pair with buddy for code reviews. Buddy should be cross-discipline (ML infra <-> product).
- Manager weekly 1:1s: progress, roadblocks, risk of blockers.

Weeks 5-8: Increase scope
- Ownership: take a small feature from design to deploy on staging.
- Run an internal demo: 15-minute show-and-tell of the feature.
- Evaluate learning plan and adjust skill goals.

Weeks 9-12: End-to-end responsibility
- Ownership of a small endpoint: capacity planning, SLO docs, dashboard creation.
- Final 90d review (documented): impact, blockers, promotions/compments next steps.

People Ops ongoing actions
- Weekly check-ins during first 8 weeks with manager & people ops rep.
- Escalation path for access delays (ticket HR-ACCESS-xxx).
- Diversity & inclusion: ensure candidate panel includes at least one interviewer from non-hiring pod.

4) Operational rubrics and checklists (quick references)
- Interviewer etiquette: start on time, read candidate notes, avoid interrupting, leave 10m buffer after interview to write notes.
- Feedback window: submit rubric within 24 hours. Default to "conditional" if you need more data rather than fail.
- Confidentiality: don’t share candidate code outside review panel.

Open questions / gambits (notes to self)
- Should we standardize the take-home to include a small KV-caching exercise? Pros: shows infra thinking. Cons: increases time burden for candidate. Action: discuss with Diego + Samir by 2025-11-19.
- How to signal readiness for on-call for new hires? Propose a shadow week after week 6. Open for debate.

Decision log (minimal)
- 2025-11-03: decided to target 3-stage loop with optional take-home for seniors (A. Patel)
- 2025-11-10: added security/PII gating to pass criteria (H. Lee)

Quick TODOs (owner tags)
- [Asha] Flesh out take-home repo skeleton + Docker setup (due 2025-11-18)
- [Diego] Draft comp guideline for ML infra senior role and share with People Ops (due 2025-11-15)
- [Samir] Confirm panel diversity checklist and add two additional reviewers (due 2025-11-20)

Appendix: sample interviewer prompts (copyable)
- System design: "Design a low-latency inference API for short text responses (<=512 tokens). How would you handle batching, cache, and per-tenant rate limits?"
- Debugging pair: "This service times out under odd bursts — here's a small failing test and logs. Find root cause and propose fix."
- Behavioral: "Tell me about a time you changed an API contract in prod. How did you communicate and rollback if needed?"

Notes to self (rough)
- Keep take-home time under 3 hours, include clear rubric.
- Make sure recruiter message includes candidate's expected bandwidth for take-home and whether they want company laptop during week 1.

End of draft.
